why: "Is this panel open?" reduced to "does it lack its hidden class" -- true before this contract, and wrong the moment a surface keeps that class off for the whole crossfade out. This is a real defect this branch hit and fixed, not a hypothetical: during those 150ms the bare check answers "open" for a screen the player has already left, which fired Customize's and Controllers' close callbacks a SECOND time when setState's unconditional close followed a Back button through the same window. Those callbacks build and dispose a live WebGL preview and add/remove window gamepad listeners, so a duplicate is a leak rather than a cosmetic slip -- and no timer count can see it, because the extra work is callbacks, not timers. `leaks no timers and fires no duplicate callbacks under repeated fast navigation` is the case that measures it, asserting opens equals closes equals 4 across a four-round burst. Scoped to hud.test.ts; expectFailures counts that scoped run only. Re-measured at hud.controls.test.ts once #318's layer cases joined the file: both Escape cases and the fake-host mirror case also count a close callback that this mutation doubles. Pinned by name since the hud suite was split (issue #511); its killers live in hud.controls.test.ts, hud.navigation.test.ts, hud.surfaces.test.ts.
killedBy: createHud application transition contract leaks no timers and fires no duplicate callbacks under repeated fast navigation
